## R10 revised: build a tool when it pays (finding 1)

The sealed policy wrote a tool for every non-trivial edit, analysis or check,
even when an existing test or check already proved the work, which competes
with reuse first and proportional effort. Owner ruling: the AGENTS.md line
becomes "Use existing deterministic tools and checks where they suffice.
Build a rerunnable tool when it materially reduces repeated work or supplies
proof a reviewer needs, and keep its output", followed by the unchanged
script-over-fanout sentence (`AGENTS.md:43-46`).

Under T5 this is an adaptation of both policy rows: the line delivers neither
`tool-over-hand-work` (a tool for all non-trivial work) nor `scripted-proof`
(a script preferred for every proof) whole. Both now adopt into one new
variant, `tool-when-it-pays`, whose `distinct_from` names both; one trait,
since the line is one mechanism (reuse first, build when it pays, keep the
output). `script-over-fanout` is delivered unchanged and keeps its row in
the original. `build-a-lever`'s description and the router row
(`mvp-mode/SKILL.md`, Skills by situation) are narrowed to match: a tool when
it saves repeated work or supplies missing proof, never by default. Its
technique traits are unchanged.

Both rows are `absent` with the variant under `also_in`: the comparison
counts a variant only in the compared skill (none here), so the adopt is
pending although the line is in place, and its completion follows at once.

## R15 revised: independent work, and an honest guide verdict (finding 4)

`-amend2` recorded `guide: ok` on the delegation default while its own text
conceded that C-14 limits Opus delegation to sizeable independent tasks.
Owner ruling: the router line says "hand independent work to a subagent";
nothing else in it changes (`.claude/skills/mvp-mode/SKILL.md:35-39`). That
narrows the mechanism, so under README §4a it is a new variant,
`delegate-independent-by-default`; `delegate-by-default` keeps its meaning
and stays defined for the history that adopted into it.

The guide verdict is now `conflict` [U-07, C-14]: the line meets C-14's
independence condition and keeps small work and verification local, but
delegating mid-sized independent work by default departs from "only sizeable
tasks". The owner keeps the default anyway, and the row records that as an
owner override with the ruling and its date, a representation the guide-check
contract now has (README §5c). GUIDE §0: the guide does not by itself change
repository policy; the override records the departure rather than hiding it.
